From the graph, the circle has center  
\[
C=(-1,1)
\]

\[
P=(3,1).

Let \(Q=(x,y)\) be either tangency point (\(U\) or \(V\)). Since \(CQ\) is perpendicular to the tangent \(PQ\),
\[
(Q-C)\cdot(P-Q)=0.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
(Q-C)\cdot(P-C)-|Q-C|^2=0.
\]
Now \(P-C=(3-(-1),1-1)=(4,0)\) and \(|Q-C|^2=r^2=4\). Thus
\[
(x+1,y-1)\cdot(4,0)-4=0,
\]
\[
4(x+1)-4=0 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x=0.
\]
Both tangency points have \(x=0\), so the line through them is the \(y\)-axis.

\[
\boxed{x=0\quad\text{(the \(y\)-axis)}}
